It was for “Lady in the Lake,” a Phillip Marlowe detective story I saw on opening day in 1947 at New York’s old Capitol Theater on Broadway. As a little kid smitten with movies, I’d been intrigued by what was billed as the first feature shot entirely with subjective camera. Yet the film turned out to be plodding and boring. No one can accuse “Hardcore Henry” of being plodding.
